summary.headline: Tinna Rubber Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to over 18% on revenue of INR157 crores, up 22% YoY, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25%.
summary.overview: Management reported record tire processing volumes in FY26 and a standalone EBITDA margin of 17.2%, up 286 bps. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY and 13% QoQ to INR157 crores, with EBITDA up 63% YoY to INR29 crores. Subsidiaries and new projects (Oman, South Africa, Saudi, TP Buildtech, PCMB, pyrolysis and rCB) carried start-up costs and geopolitical drag that management expects to normalise through FY27. Infra segment softened on bitumen shortages, which management expects to be temporary.

financial_highlights.value: revenue INR75 crores, EBITDA INR6 crores

financial_highlights.metric: Combined loss, Mbodla, South Africa and Tinna Rubber Arabia (FY26)

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% YoY in FY26, driven by MRP and reclaim rubber demand and exports, which grew 30% in volume. Management sees strong FY27 growth on higher virgin polymer prices and rubber blending in bitumen.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue declined from INR222 crores to INR205 crores in FY26 as the company prioritised value-added products. Bitumen shortage is expected to hit Q1-Q2 FY27 volumes, with management expecting normalisation later in the year.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23% in FY26 despite a marginal volume decline, reflecting price correction. Management expects a modest improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Revenue stable YoY while volumes rose 8%. Appointed exclusive distributor in India for Zibo TAA Metal Technology (China) steel abrasives, with 30% volume growth targeted in FY27.

segments.name: PCMB (polymer compounding and masterbatch)
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 turnover, operating at 40% utilisation, with QoQ growth of about 75%. Budgeted FY27 revenue of about INR75 crores, rising to 8-10% of revenue. Haryana polymer compounding capacity to reach 18,000 tpa by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Pyrolysis (TPO) and rCB
segments.commentary: Pyrolysis plant has started and the rCB plant is under commissioning. FY27 revenue from both is projected at INR50-55 crores, with EBITDA margins of 15-19%. Full operation is expected by Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 20-25% over FY26.
Vision 2029 target: revenue of INR1,000 crores with EBITDA margin above 18%; management says 18% is its guidance comfort level, and the FY29 target is organic only.
Maintain about 18% EBITDA margin in FY27; consolidated EBITDA projected to cross INR100 crores in FY27.
Tire-crush capacity to rise from 185,000 tpa to 235,000 tpa by FY27, with about INR100 crores capex over FY27-28, mostly from internal accruals and up to about INR20 crores debt if needed.
Oman normalisation expected within Q1 FY27; South Africa breakeven from Q2 FY27; Saudi tire recycling plant (24,000 tpa) capex of INR20-25 crores, with work starting end Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Working capital days expected to stay at current levels, since PCMB carries higher credit terms.
capex_capacity: Tire-crush capacity in India expanded 9% to 185,000 tons in FY26; target of 235,000 tpa by FY27. Tire-crush volume rose 13% to 155,000 tons in FY26.
Capacity utilisation was 90% in India and 85% in Oman in FY26. Varale plant at 80% utilisation.
Solar capacity rose from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW in FY26; about 50% of power needs expected from renewables from FY27.
Pyrolysis plant (100 TPD feed) and rCB plant: about INR40 crores capex, largely complete. TPO stabilisation expected by end Q1 FY27 and rCB trial production in Q2 FY27.
TP Buildtech Kolkata plant commissioned, running under 25% utilisation, with three new construction system product lines launched.
Micronized rubber powder capacity being increased at at least two plants. PCMB capacity moving from a 6,000 tpa pilot to an 18,000 tpa polymer compounding facility in Haryana.
demand_pricing: Raw material economics: virgin rubber about INR240-260/kg vs recycled rubber about INR50/kg, roughly one-fifth the cost.

Bitumen prices have almost doubled, driving stronger crumb-rubber-modified bitumen (CRMB) demand, though India's bitumen supply constraint (imports of 3-3.5 million tons) hit road-work volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP improved on demand; management said realisation volatility currently favours the company.
Freight rates and elevated polymer prices from the Middle East crisis raised import costs; management says the company offset these by sourcing from multiple geographies and feedstock types.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants: management cites a moat from raw material, product, customer and geographic diversity, plus 2-5 year approval cycles with tire majors.

qa_highlights.question: Vision FY29 revenue breakup by segment, and EPR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PCMB rises toward 8-10% of revenue from about 4%. Infra is expected to be about 30%, Industrial about 35%, Consumer about 10%, with the balance from rCB and pyrolysis. EPR revenue stays around INR29-30 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the infra slowdown hit blended margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects better realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP to offset any infra softness, and says the bitumen-driven slowdown is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA expected from RCB and pyrolysis plants in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined FY27 revenue of about INR50-55 crores. EBITDA margins of 15-19% are expected once the plants are fully running, with payback in line with the existing business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 42 to 55?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly due to PCMB, where industry practice carries longer credit days. Core rubber-products credit days have not changed materially, and working capital days are expected to stay at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crore capex be funded, and what is the debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it from internal accruals, with FY27 EBITDA projected above INR100 crores. Management may take up to about INR20 crores of debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling bitumen supply and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds no bitumen and does not trade it. It supplies modifier to IOC and to contractors who source their own bitumen, which the company says is assured business for the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Bitumen availability (India imports 3-3.5 million tons, with Iran a key supplier) may keep infra volumes soft in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Middle East tensions delay the Saudi plant capital works (now expected end Q2 or Q3 FY27) and disrupt Oman exports; Oman normalisation is expected within Q1 FY27.
Start-up losses at South Africa and new plants; South Africa breakeven targeted from Q2 FY27, and TP Buildtech margins remain under pressure from crude, polymer and currency movements.
Receivable days rose to about 55 from 42 due to PCMB credit terms; watch whether working capital intensity persists.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants; management cites strong moats but no quantified pricing impact.
Consolidated PAT growth (9%) lagged EBITDA growth; FY26 revenue growth was only 8% and infra revenue fell, so FY27 20-25% growth needs execution.
key_quotes: FY26 was another year of strong execution for Tinna Rubber, despite geopolitical uncertainties and a dynamic operating environment, we achieved record tire processing volumes and delivered robust EBITDA margins of over 17%.
But we expect that to normalize immediately because India has a very aggressive program for road construction.
Our comfort level to give a guidance to market is at 18%.

I don't see us doing any inorganic acquisition related to our business, but some adjacency business, if it comes across, where we have something new to learn or a new product line to add or new geography to add, those are the ideas we remain open to and we will look at those opportunities.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 execution, Vision 2029 and the Industrial/PCMB growth story, but cautious and deflecting on infra near-term volumes, bitumen supply, and per-ton realisation metrics. Management repeatedly stressed temporary disruption and declined to disclose new expansion locations or quantify pricing impact from competition.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%) and ~18% EBITDA margin, backed by tire-crush capacity rising 27% to 235,000 tpa by FY27 (INR100 crore capex over FY27-28), PCMB to 18,000 tpa, and pyrolysis/rCB guided at INR50-55 crore FY27 revenue; bitumen shortage is a near-term headwind to Infra in Q1-Q2 FY27, and no order book figures were given.
